newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Aug retail sales fall 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Aug retail sales fall 0.4 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales fell 0.4 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted C$17.86 billion from C$17.94 billion in July, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a -0.6 +0.5 C$13.60 bln
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast that seasonally adjusted retail sales would rise by 0.4 percent in August.
The agency said employment and trade fell by 0.4 percent in September, but preliminary indications pointed to a rise in motor vehicle sales in September.
Statistics Canada also revised the figure for July's seasonally adjusted sales to C$17.94 billion from C$17.98 billion.

Statistics Canada said retail sales rose 1.4 percent in the first eight months of the year from the same period in 1995. But with the effect of price changes removed, sales were 0.1 percent lower, the agency said.
"This contrasts with the good performance of exports, as reflected in other economic sectors such as manufacturing and wholesaling," Statistics Canada said.
The agency said the largest decreases in dollar terms in August came from a 4.1 percent drop in drug sales and a 0.4 percent decline in food retail sales.
Sales rose in the furniture, automotive and general merchandise sectors.
